A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GScenes research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original GScenes reconstruction experiments on MipNeRF360 and DL3DV, component ablations, and pose-estimation errors.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds pose-sensitivity and training-view reconstruction studies in Appendices G and H.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 2.1–2.7 retain the initialization, RGBD diffusion, FiLM conditioning, confidence measure, and Gaussian optimization procedure. Correcting DUSt3r to MASt3r in the pose-table caption agrees with v2's existing method description.

E1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the training data sources and MipNeRF360, DL3DV-10K, and CO3D evaluation coverage. The added studies examine pose inputs and training-view fidelity within the existing DL3DV reconstruction task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the corresponding main comparisons and ablations is unchanged. Appendix G varies pose inputs for the existing DiffusioNeRF baseline, while Appendix H reuses MASt3R + 3DGS.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds a three-scene DiffusioNeRF control using MASt3R-estimated rather than dense COLMAP training poses. Appendix H evaluates PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS on Square's training views with 3, 6, and 9 inputs. Existing main protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted analyses of DiffusioNeRF's sensitivity to estimated poses and generative priors' effect on input-view fidelity, including a one-scene quantitative study. Existing conditioning, confidence-map, and autoencoder analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without run-to-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results follow this practice, with no new seed or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the retained pose-error table have unchanged values. New Table 4 reports GScenes PSNR of 22.44/21.52/21.70 versus MASt3R + 3DGS's 23.34/22.32/22.96 on Square's 3/6/9 training-view splits. Figures 16–17 add qualitative pose-sensitivity and fidelity findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the other mathematical definitions are retained, including confidence estimation, FiLM modulation, diffusion guidance, and reconstruction losses. No new proofs or formal derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient pose-free scene reconstruction, RGBD diffusion priors, FiLM and confidence conditioning, and competitive reconstruction performance.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly connects unresolved generated-view inconsistencies to floaters and reduced input-view fidelity. Figure 13 refines the generic competitive-performance description to better or similar ReconFusion examples and slightly worse CAT3D quality. Existing limitations move from Appendix G to I.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page address described as providing code, videos, and additional results. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and training and reconstruction timings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds citations to Viewset Diffusion and Denoising Diffusion via Image-Based Rendering, including IB-planes among prior representations. The main novelty and research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v3 condenses Section 2's roadmap, makes light language and citation-format edits, and adds publication information, updated author contacts, and acknowledgements. New Appendices G/H precede the relocated limitations; the broader narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 16–17 and Table 4, expands Figure 13's caption, and relocates the former pose-error Table 4 as Table 5. Publication headers and modest reflow change the layout; existing visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices G/H provide direct evidence of pose sensitivity and quantify a training-view fidelity cost, improving the paper's support and transparency about limitations. These studies cover three scenes and one scene respectively, while the central method and main benchmark evidence remain unchanged, making the overall gain limited.
